extracted.intended_audience: Reviewers for CVPR 2017 (members of the CVPR Reviewing Committee)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and procedural rules for reviewing papers submitted to the CVPR 2017 main conference, including ethical responsibilities, evaluation criteria (novelty, soundness, impact), and how to use the CMT review system. Applies to writing both preliminary and final reviews and participating in rebuttal/discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blind Reviews / Anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors were asked to take reasonable efforts to hide their identities, including not listing their names or affiliations and omitting acknowledgments. Reviewers should also make all efforts to keep their identity invisible to the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Author Guidelines for details on how authors have been instructed to preserve anonymity, including guidelines for referencing one's own prior work. Review papers independently as if arXiv papers didn't exist; treat papers fairly whether or not you know (or suspect) who wrote them. New examples in Reviewer FAQs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check your assigned papers for conflicts and comfort
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you get your reviewing assignment, please go through all the papers to make sure that (a) there is no obvious conflict with you (e.g., a paper authored by your recent collaborator from a different institution) and (b) you feel comfortable to review the paper assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If either issue arises, email the Program Chairs immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: What to Look For: novelty, potential impact, and technical soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for what's good or stimulating in the paper. CVPR as a conference is looking for new ideas. Acceptance and rejection decisions should not be determined solely by the method's raw performance. Each paper that is accepted should be technically sound and make a contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embrace novel, brave concepts even if not tested on many datasets; weigh both the novelty and potential impact of the work alongside the reported performance. Not exceeding state-of-the-art on benchmarks is not grounds for rejection by itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Specific in critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Your main critique of the paper should be written in terms of a list of strengths and weaknesses of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bullet points and explain your arguments. Be specific and detailed; simply saying 'this is well known' or 'common practice' is not sufficient—cite specific publications, books, or public disclosures. Your discussion, sometimes more than your score, helps authors, fellow reviewers, and Area Chairs understand your basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide actionable suggestions for improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should include specific feedback on ways the authors can improve their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggestions may be very specific (e.g., recommending a numerical solver) or more general (new dataset, new application area, generalization ideas). Be generous about giving new ideas that help the authors and the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Destroy review materials after use
rubrics_metrics.description: When you have finished with your review, you should destroy any paper manuscript and/or supporting material you received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ethics guidelines for full confidentiality handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and professionalism in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The tone of your review is important. A harshly written review will be disregarded by the authors, regardless of whether your criticisms are true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word your review diplomatically while staying true to your thoughts. Put yourself in the mindset of writing to someone you wish to help (e.g., a respected colleague). Avoid belittling or sarcastic comments; write courteous, informative, incisive, and helpful reviews you would be proud to add your name to (were it not anonymous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer spirit and careful deliberation
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach your reviews in the spirit of volunteerism; your reviews make you a gatekeeper in deciding which papers are ready for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read a paper and think about it over several days before writing the review. Take enough time to write a thoughtful and detailed review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short reviews are unhelpful
rubrics_metrics.description: Short reviews are unhelpful to authors, other reviewers, and Area Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have agreed to review a paper, you should take enough time to write a thoughtful and detailed review rather than a short/insufficient one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific about writing clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific when you suggest that the writing needs to be improved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a particular section is unclear, point it out and give suggestions for how it can be clarified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not request citations to your own work
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't give away your identity by asking the authors to cite several of your own papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid requesting self-citations that would identify you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support claims about prior work and novelty with references
rubrics_metrics.description: Be specific about novelty. Claims in a review that the submitted work 'has been done before' MUST be backed up with specific references and an explanation of how closely they are related.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For positive reviews, summarize the novel aspects that are most interesting in the strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of arXiv (preprint) papers
rubrics_metrics.description: ArXiv papers are not considered prior work since they have not been peer reviewed. Review your CVPR papers independently as if the arXiv papers didn't exist. Citations to these papers are not required and failing to cite or beat performance of arXiv papers are not grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific prohibitions/examples: It is NOT OK to suggest rejection for not citing an arXiv paper or not being better than something on arXiv; NOT OK to accept solely because it outperforms an arXiv paper; NOT OK to reject solely because it performs worse than something on arXiv; NOT OK to regard arXiv as the standard for state of the art. It IS OK to suggest authors should acknowledge/be aware of something on arXiv; it IS OK for an author to decline to acknowledge arXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: If out-of-scope, explain and suggest alternative venues
rubrics_metrics.description: If you think the paper is out of scope for CVPR's subject areas, clearly explain why in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to the Call for Papers and suggest other publication possibilities (journals, conferences, workshops) better matched to the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using 'you' — refer to 'the authors' or 'the paper'
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid referring to the authors by using the phrase 'you'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases should be replaced by 'the authors' or 'the paper' to avoid confrontational tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect confidentiality of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: As a reviewer you have the responsibility to protect the confidentiality of the ideas represented in the papers you review. CVPR submissions are not published documents and may be considered new or proprietary by the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not show the paper to anyone else unless they are asked to write/help with the review; do not show results, videos, images, or supplementary material to non-reviewers; do not use ideas from papers you review to develop new ones; after review, destroy copies and erase any implementations/results you produced to evaluate the ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important for you to avoid any conflict of interest. There should be absolutely no question about the impartiality of any review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflicts include (but are not limited to): same institution as one of the authors; having been directly involved in the work; situations others might perceive as a conflict; having collaborated with one of the authors in the past three years; being the MS/PhD advisor or advisee of an author. If you recognize a conflict, return the paper and do not submit a review; email the Program Chairs so someone else can be found to review it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for submission rule violations on assigned papers
rubrics_metrics.description: When you download papers, check for possible conflict or submission rule violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations include over 8 pages (not including references), constituting a double submission, supplementary material including a newer version of the paper. Specify the exact nature of the violation and contact the Program Chairs immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the review form and assign preliminary rating properly
rubrics_metrics.description: For a paper, enter a review in CMT and assign a Preliminary Rating using the review form which contains detailed instructions and the meaning of different ratings (Oral, Poster, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save as draft if unfinished (visible only to you). To make the review visible to the Area Chair, click 'Submit'; 'Submit' won't work if any of the required items is not filled. CMT restricts certain characters; introducing spaces in special characters (e.g. 'y < x') can be a workaround.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional offline reviewing workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: You can review papers offline using provided review template files that can be downloaded and edited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download one review template file per paper; edit only fields currently filled with 'REPLACE THIS WITH YOUR ANSWER'. Be careful not to add characters interpretable as HTML tags; upload will overwrite the current review. Verify the review after uploading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in post-rebuttal discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: After the rebuttal period, reviewers will work with Area Chairs to clear up any confusions and attempt to reach consensus on papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CMT bulletin board feature where Area Chairs can post notes anonymously; reviewers will be notified and identities of reviewers are hidden from each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter final recommendation after rebuttal and discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: After the rebuttal period you will enter your final recommendation on CMT. This may differ from your preliminary rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final recommendation should reflect your judgment taking into account all other reviews, the authors' rebuttal, and the discussion about the paper (if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: No quota-based acceptance/rejection — evaluate each paper independently
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no minimum number of papers you should accept or reject. Each paper should be evaluated in its own right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT assume that your stack of papers should have the same acceptance rate as the entire conference. If most assigned papers have value, accept them; if many are weak, provide clear and very specific comments for rejection.
